sections.en: BNB is changing hands near $785.05, +4.68% over the past 24 hours and +8.94% on a 7-day view. Spot trades above the 50-day average ($691.55) and above the 200-day average ($682.51), keeping the medium-term structure constructive. The 30-day tape reads as a recovery phase (+12.78%), suggesting the market is still repairing.

sections.en: Total market capitalization stands near $104.5B (CoinGecko). Reported 24-hour spot volume is $1.40B with 7-day average turnover broadly normal versus the trailing month (1.07x) . Note: the ETF-flow and sentiment figures above are the public Farside and alternative.me series; proprietary on-chain datasets are still left out rather than estimated. The alternative.me Fear & Greed gauge prints 70 (Greed).

**Derivatives positioning.** The public Binance futures endpoints did not answer for this asset on this cycle, so rather than fabricate a view the desk flags it as a **data gap**: funding and open-interest extremes remain the standard trigger for squeeze dynamics in BNB.

**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is perfect bullish alignment (price > EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200), the textbook configuration of a trend-following regime where pullbacks into the 20-day mean tend to be bought. Spot at $784.59 versus EMA20 $733.46, EMA50 $691.55 and EMA200 $682.51 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $772.35 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $688.25 as the 2σ downside envelope; upper band $784.22 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $21.80 implies a typical daily range of roughly 2.8 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 70.0 — overbought territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits above its signal line (23.14 vs 20.81, histogram +2.338), consistent with building momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 42%; the 20-day band spans 13% of the mid — compressed, which often precedes a volatility expansion; 7-day turnover runs at 1.07x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned +12.78% over 30 days and +35.84% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (+8.94%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en:
**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires continued holds of the 50-day average ($691.55); RSI holding above 60 (currently 70). Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $772.35. In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on BNB: spot $785.05 with the medium-term bias constructive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (+4.68%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
